name: FERAL FEMME
tagline: Two subjects. One machine. Same refusal to consent.
standard: Written to be verified, not agreed with.
description: FERAL FEMME investigates every industry built on a body that could not agree to it — holding animals and women at equal weight. Public-record reporting, reframed with attribution, across ten industries, with free sustainability tools.

shop.note: `buy` is a PayPal no-code checkout link, created the same way as the donate ones — one per product, with the price fixed on PayPal's side. Leave it empty and the button falls back to an enquiry email, so the page is publishable before the links exist.
shop.processorNote: Priced and charged in US dollars, which is what the PayPal links are issued in. Your bank sets the rate on the day.
shop.delivery: The file is emailed to the address on your PayPal receipt, usually within a few hours and always within one working day. It is sent by a person, not a robot, which is also how you get told when an edition changes.

services.headline: Claims review
services.summary: If you sell something and say it is better, someone will eventually ask you to prove it. Increasingly that someone is a regulator.

tiers.name: Claim Check
tiers.detail: One claim, or one product page. A short verdict with the regulatory basis behind it. The low-risk way to see the work before committing to more.

tiers.name: Claims Review
tiers.detail: Full website and packaging copy for one brand. Every claim marked defensible, needs substantiation, or do not use — with the rule it runs into and wording that survives.

tiers.name: Certification & Supply Audit
tiers.detail: What your certifications actually cover against what they imply, plus supplier-tier risk. Drawn from the same database that powers the public decoders.

tiers.name: Standing retainer
tiers.detail: Campaign copy reviewed before it ships rather than after a regulator does. Capped at a set number of reviews a month.

services.invoiceNote: Quoted and invoiced in rand, because the work is invoiced directly rather than sold through a checkout. Clients outside South Africa are quoted the equivalent in their own currency on request — ask before you assume the rand figure is the whole answer.
checks: The EU Green Claims Directive and the Empowering Consumers Directive.
The UK Competition and Markets Authority's Green Claims Code.
The published scope of any certification you cite — which is usually narrower than the logo implies.
The documented record of the suppliers and parent companies behind the product.

positioning.lede: We investigate every industry built on a body that could not agree to it — and we hold animals and women at equal weight. Neither is a metaphor for the other. Both are literal.
positioning.body: The cruelty is rarely called cruelty. It is called tradition, testing, farming, research, wellness, self-care. We translate the vocabulary, cite the source, and file the receipt — across fashion, food, beauty, wildlife, medicine, tech, and the advertising that obscures all of it.

method.title: Public-Record Reporting
method.body: Field notes summarise investigations that already exist in the public record — the Sunday Times, the Guardian, Reuters, AP, the New York Times, the Bureau of Investigative Journalism, peer-reviewed studies, parliamentary inquiries, regulatory filings.

method.title: Editorial Synthesis
method.body: Each source is read, reframed in Feral Femme's restrained editorial voice, and connected to the broader pattern of the industry it documents. The original publisher always gets the credit.

method.title: AI-Directed Editorial Imagery
method.body: The archive's visual essays are created using AI image generation, directed by Ayden Rosemary Brown. Each image is a deliberate frame — conceptual editorial work, not documentary photography.

method.title: Sustainability Tools
method.body: Nine free interactive tools turn awareness into practice — from the Wardrobe Wear Counter and the Plant Plate Tracker to the Ingredient, Greenwashing, Certification, and Material decoders.

method.title: The Research Briefing
method.body: Every field note is sent to subscribers in full on the day it is published, through a provider that reads the site’s own feed. No separate edition, and nothing in the email that is not on the site.

method.title: Self-Funded Platform
method.body: Feral Femme is independently funded through reader donations. No advertisers, no industry sponsorship, no editorial conflicts of interest.

newsletter.name: The Research Briefing
newsletter.summary: Every field note in full, sent the day it is published — the whole note, not a summary with a link back. No promotions, no product recommendations, one-click unsubscribe.
newsletter.confirmText: Thank you — check your inbox to confirm your subscription.
newsletter.note: `action` is MailerLite embedded form 197500769051608208 on account 2610955, posted to assets.mailerlite.com rather than the dashboard.mailerlite.com address MailerLite's own share page carries: that one 301s here, and fetch downgrades a POST to a GET when it follows a 301, which would drop the address. `emailField` and `fields` are the names that endpoint expects. The form has double opt-in on, which is why `confirmText` tells the reader to confirm. `group` is the list the form feeds and the briefing sends to; `automationStart` is the cutover before which no note is ever mailed. Clearing `action` degrades the form to a mailto: link.

donate.headline: Fund the research directly
donate.summary: Feral Femme is self-funded and reader-supported. A donation funds independent investigative work with no strings attached — no advertisers, no industry sponsorship, no editorial conflicts of interest.
donate.processorNote: PayPal charges in USD. Your bank sets the final rate.

amounts.label: Supporter
amounts.detail: Contributes toward source-database access and hosting.

amounts.label: Contributor
amounts.detail: Goes toward source-database access and the editorial research behind the field notes.

amounts.label: Sustainer
amounts.detail: Goes toward research time, paywalled reporting, and keeping every note free to read.

amounts.label: Patron
amounts.detail: Goes toward the standing costs — database subscriptions, archive access, hosting — that the platform carries whether or not anyone gives.

custom.label: Any other amount
custom.detail: Name your own figure at checkout.

donate.note: Each amount carries its own PayPal payment link, because a no-code checkout link has its amount fixed on PayPal's side and ignores one appended to the URL. `donate.link` is the fallback for a PayPal.me or hosted-button URL, which do take an appended amount. With neither set, the page renders an enquiry mailto: rather than a dead button.

analytics.note: The previous build loaded Google Analytics. It is disabled here by default: set `provider` to 'ga4' to re-enable it, and disclose it on /privacy/ first. Left empty, no third-party script is emitted.
